t.1.172.1: The Gandharva said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, that brahmin seer restrained his own anger from the destruction of all the worlds.
t.1.172.2: And then that greatly splendid seer Parāśara, son of Śakti, foremost among all who know the Vedas, performed a sacrifice with a sacrificial session for the destruction of the Rākṣasas.
t.1.172.3: Then that great sage, remembering the slaying of Śakti, burned the Rākṣasas, old and young alike, in the sacrifice he had spread out.
t.1.172.4: For Vasiṣṭha did not restrain him from the slaughter of the Rākṣasas, being resolved: "Let me not break his second vow."
t.1.172.5: At that sacrificial session the great sage stood before the three blazing fires like a fourth fire.
t.1.172.6: By that brilliant sacrifice, offered according to proper method, the sky was illumined, as if by the sun at the end of the rainy season.
t.1.172.7: All the sages there, Vasiṣṭha and the others, regarded him, blazing with splendor in the sky, as if he were a second sun.
t.1.172.8: Then the noble-minded seer Atri, wishing to bring that sattra to its close, approached him, who was supremely difficult for others to approach.
t.1.172.10: But Pulastya, O bull among the Bharatas, because of the slaughter of those Rākṣasas, spoke these words, O Pārtha, to Parāśara, the subduer of enemies.
t.1.172.9: Likewise Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu came to that great sacrifice, O slayer of foes, desiring to save the lives of the Rākṣasas.
t.1.172.11: Is all going without hindrance for you, my dear? Do you rejoice, little son, in the slaughter of all the rakṣases, who were unknowing and blameless?
t.1.172.13: And those sons of the great sage Vasiṣṭha, Śakti and the younger ones, are all filled with joy and rejoice together with the gods. All this is indeed known to Vasiṣṭha, O great sage.
t.1.172.12: O Parāśara, best of soma-drinkers, though you are most excellent, you are bringing upon me this entire, most unrighteous extermination of offspring. And King Kalmāṣapāda wishes to ascend to heaven.
t.1.172.15: Thus addressed by Pulastya and by the wise Vasiṣṭha, Parāśara, the son of Śakti, then brought the sacrificial session to its close.
t.1.172.14: This is the annihilation of the rākṣasas and of ascetics, dear son, and you have become the instrument of it in this sacrifice, O joy of the descendants of Vasiṣṭha. Abandon this sattra; good fortune to you; let it be concluded for you.
t.1.172.16: The sage released the fire he had gathered for the sacrifice of all the Rākṣasas into a great forest on the northern slope of Himavat.
t.1.172.17: That fire is seen there even today, always at every parvan, devouring Rākṣasas, trees, and stones as well.
